gloss: realis form; perfective base (classical Japanese grammar)

definitions.explanation: A conjugation form in classical Japanese grammar that indicates the action has already been realized or completed. In modern grammar, this form has been reclassified as the hypothetical form ({仮定形|かていけい}), but the term {已然形|いぜんけい} is still used when discussing classical texts.

examples.japanese: {已然形|いぜんけい}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{古典|こてん}→古典：00242_koten⟧⟦{文法|ぶんぽう}→文法：01506_bunpou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{用語|ようご}→用語：04086_yougo⟧だ。
examples.english: The realis form is a term from classical grammar.

examples.japanese: {已然形|いぜんけい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧「ば」⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{付|つ}く→付く：01960_tsuku⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{確定|かくてい}→確定：13707_kakutei⟧⟦{条件|じょうけん}→条件：03285_jouken⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{表|あらわ}す→表す：01868_arawasu⟧。
examples.english: When ば is attached to the realis form, it expresses a definite condition.

examples.japanese: ⟦{現代|げんだい}→現代：02722_gendai⟧⟦{文法|ぶんぽう}→文法：01506_bunpou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{仮定形|かていけい}→仮定形：24811_kateikei⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{呼|よ}ばれる→呼ぶ：00766_yobu⟧⟦{形|かたち}→形：02193_katachi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{古典|こてん}→古典：00242_koten⟧⟦{文法|ぶんぽう}→文法：01506_bunpou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{已然形|いぜんけい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{相当|そうとう}する→相当する：21146_soutousuru⟧。
examples.english: The form called the hypothetical form in modern grammar corresponds to the realis form in classical grammar.

notes:
A grammatical term from classical Japanese (⟦{古典|こてん}→古典：00242_koten⟧⟦{文法|ぶんぽう}→文法：01506_bunpou⟧). The character {已|い} means "already," so {已然形|いぜんけい} literally means "the form for what has already happened." In classical Japanese, this form followed by ば expressed a realized condition ("since/because X happened"), unlike the modern hypothetical use ("if X").

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {已然形|いぜんけい}＋ば: realis form + ba (confirmed condition)
- ⟦{六|ろく}→六：00747_roku⟧{活用形|かつようけい}: the six conjugation forms (of which {已然形|いぜんけい} is one)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{仮定形|かていけい}→仮定形：24811_kateikei⟧: hypothetical form — the modern grammar equivalent; expresses "if" rather than "since"
- ⟦{未然形|みぜんけい}→未然形：23610_mizenkei⟧: irrealis form — the opposite conjugation base, expressing what has not yet happened
